issues.body: `_model_target_checkout_ref` counts only a literal unquoted `path: target` line. YAML scalars such as `path: "target"` (or `path: 'target'`) materialize the same directory for `actions/checkout` but do not set `is_target`. An adversarial workflow mutation can insert the correctly pinned, unquoted decoy tested here, change the real model checkout to `path: "target"`, and revert its `ref` to the moving default branch. The extractor sees exactly one match and returns the decoy's expected ref; the producer checks and action pinning remain green, while the later quoted-path checkout overwrites the model working tree with the unbound revision. Thus the round-2 mutually masking duplicate remains possible through semantically equivalent YAML.
issues.fix_hint: Determine target checkout uniqueness from parsed YAML values, or normalize and validate supported scalar spellings before comparison, then fail closed unless exactly one checkout step resolves to destination `target`. Add a mutant with a pinned unquoted decoy plus a real checkout using quoted `path: "target"` and a moving/default ref, and require `<ambiguous>` or another refusal. Include both single- and double-quoted equivalents so the assertion tests semantic value rather than one textual representation.
issues.title: Raw path spelling still lets an equivalent target checkout evade uniqueness

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-2 exact decoy mutant is now rejected, but the uniqueness check still compares raw YAML spelling rather than the parsed checkout destination. A second checkout can materialize the same `target` directory using an equivalent quoted scalar while remaining invisible to `nmatch`; the exact-spelling decoy can then satisfy the expected-ref guard while the checkout actually consumed by later steps is unbound. This is materially the same major masking finding as round 2, so progress is stagnant.
